issues.description: After clicking 'Create account', the system displays a 'Registration completed' message, but it's unclear how long it will take to receive the verification email. Users might be unsure if the process is still running or if there's an issue.
issues.recommendation: Add a loading indicator or a brief message like 'Sending verification email...' while the email is being sent. Also, provide an estimated time for email arrival or instructions on what to do if the email is not received within a certain timeframe.

heuristic: Match between System and Real World

issues.description: The term "EventHelpr" itself, while functional, doesn't immediately convey the purpose of the application. A more descriptive name could improve user understanding.
issues.recommendation: Consider a name that more directly reflects the app's function, such as "GroupEventPlanner" or "EventOrganizer".

issues.description: The phrase "Enter your event key" at the bottom of the page might be confusing for new users who are not familiar with the concept of an event key. It's not immediately clear what this key is or how to obtain it.
issues.recommendation: Provide a brief explanation of what an event key is and how it's used, or rephrase it to something more user-friendly like "Enter event code" or "Join event with code".

issues.description: After creating an account, the user is taken to a "Registration completed" page that states "There is only one last step missing before you can login." However, the user is not prompted to complete this step, and the user must manually log in.
issues.recommendation: After account creation, automatically redirect the user to the login page or provide a direct link to the login page on the "Registration completed" page.

issues.description: The system allows account creation without verifying the email address first. This could lead to users creating accounts with typos in their email, preventing them from logging in later or receiving important notifications.
issues.recommendation: Implement email verification during account creation. Send a verification link to the provided email address and require users to click the link before their account is fully activated.

issues.description: The password fields do not provide any visual feedback on password strength or complexity requirements during input. Users might create weak passwords that are easily compromised.
issues.recommendation: Implement a password strength indicator that provides real-time feedback as the user types their password. Clearly display the password complexity requirements (e.g., minimum length, special characters) near the password fields.

issues.description: After registration, the user is redirected to a page stating that an email has been sent for verification. However, there is no direct link or button to check the email or resend the verification email if it's not received. This forces the user to recall the next steps (checking email, spam folder) instead of providing immediate recognition.
issues.recommendation: Add a button or link on the 'Registration completed' page that allows users to directly check their email (opens a new tab with a common email provider) or resend the verification email. This provides immediate recognition of the next steps and reduces the cognitive load on the user.

issues.description: The registration process requires email verification, which adds an extra step and can be inefficient for users who want to quickly access the platform.
issues.recommendation: Consider offering alternative registration methods, such as social login (e.g., Google, Facebook), to streamline the process for users who prefer a faster signup.

issues.description: The landing page has a busy background image that doesn't add value and can be distracting. The image is a stylized photo of a conference, which doesn't clearly communicate the app's purpose for organizing various types of events.
issues.recommendation: Replace the background image with a simpler, more abstract graphic or a solid color that aligns with the brand's color scheme. Alternatively, use a carousel of images showcasing different event types the app can help organize (e.g., travel, meetings, workshops).

issues.description: The 'My Events' page, after logging in, shows a lot of empty space and 'No entries present' messages. This creates a feeling of emptiness and doesn't immediately guide the user on what to do next.
issues.recommendation: Include a call to action button or a short tutorial on the 'My Events' page to guide new users on how to create their first event. Consider adding placeholder content or example events to demonstrate the app's functionality.

issues.description: There is no help or documentation available on the registration page to guide users through the process or explain the privacy policy.
issues.recommendation: Add a link to a help page or a tooltip next to each field on the registration form to provide context and guidance. Also, provide a clear and concise explanation of the privacy policy and how user data is handled.

issues.description: After registration, the user is informed that an email has been sent for verification, but there is no direct link to a help section if the email is not received or if the user encounters issues with the verification process.
issues.recommendation: Include a direct link to a troubleshooting guide or FAQ section on the registration confirmation page that addresses common issues related to email verification, such as checking the spam folder or requesting a new verification email.

issues.description: After clicking the "Create event" button, there is no immediate feedback to indicate that the event is being created. The user might wonder if the action was successful or if there's a delay.
issues.recommendation: Implement a loading indicator or a brief message like "Creating event..." after the "Create event" button is clicked. This provides immediate feedback to the user that the system is processing their request.

issues.description: The term "Agenda" might not be immediately clear to all users, especially those unfamiliar with event planning terminology. It could be interpreted in various ways, leading to confusion about its purpose.
issues.recommendation: Replace "Agenda" with a more descriptive and user-friendly term like "Schedule" or "Itinerary." This would provide a clearer understanding of the section's content and purpose.

issues.description: The term "Side events" might not be immediately clear to all users. It could be interpreted in various ways, leading to confusion about its purpose.
issues.recommendation: Replace "Side events" with a more descriptive and user-friendly term like "Additional events" or "Optional events." This would provide a clearer understanding of the section's content and purpose.

issues.description: There is no clear "cancel" or "reset" button on the "Create event" page. If a user starts filling out the form and decides not to create the event, there's no obvious way to discard the changes and return to the previous page without manually navigating back.
issues.recommendation: Add a "Cancel" button at the bottom of the "Create event" page, next to the "Create event" button. This button should clear all entered data and redirect the user back to the "My events" page.

issues.description: When selecting dates for the event, there is no clear way to clear the selected date. If a user accidentally selects the wrong date, they might struggle to remove it.
issues.recommendation: Add a clear "X" button next to the selected date in the date picker to allow users to easily clear the selected date.

issues.description: The date pickers for the start and end dates use different icons to clear the selected date. One uses an 'x' and the other uses a trash can icon.
issues.recommendation: Use the same icon for clearing the date in both date pickers. The 'x' is more common for clearing fields, so using that consistently would be better.

issues.description: The form allows the user to select an end date that is before the start date. This is a common error that should be prevented.
issues.recommendation: Implement a validation check to ensure the end date is not before the start date. Display an error message if the user attempts to select an invalid end date.

issues.description: The address field requires the user to search Google Maps, which might not be the most intuitive way for all users to input an address. Users might prefer a simple text field where they can directly type the address.
issues.recommendation: Provide a text field for address input in addition to the Google Maps search. This allows users to choose their preferred method of input, catering to different levels of familiarity with Google Maps.

issues.description: There are no keyboard shortcuts or advanced features readily apparent for experienced users to quickly navigate or input data. For example, date selection requires clicking through calendars, which can be time-consuming.
issues.recommendation: Implement keyboard shortcuts for common actions like date selection (e.g., typing the date directly) and navigation between sections. Consider adding a 'quick add' feature for agenda items or locations.

issues.description: The "Create event" page contains many fields and tabs, some of which might not be relevant for all users or events. This can overwhelm users and make it difficult to find the essential information.
issues.recommendation: Consider using progressive disclosure to hide less frequently used fields and tabs initially. Provide a clear way for users to access these advanced options if needed. Also, consider a step-by-step wizard to guide users through the event creation process.

issues.description: The map takes up a significant portion of the screen, even if the user doesn't need it at that moment. This can be distracting and push other important fields further down the page.
issues.recommendation: Collapse the map by default and provide a button to expand it when needed. This will reduce visual clutter and allow users to focus on other event details.

heuristic: Help Recognize, Diagnose, Recover from Errors

issues.description: There are no error messages displayed during the event creation process, even if required fields are left blank. This makes it difficult for the user to understand what information is missing or incorrect.
issues.recommendation: Implement error messages that appear when the user attempts to create an event with missing required fields. The error messages should clearly indicate which fields need to be filled in and provide guidance on the expected format or content.

issues.description: After clicking 'Save Settings' on the 'Decision Support' tab, there is no immediate visual confirmation that the settings have been saved. The user might be unsure if the action was successful.
issues.recommendation: Implement a brief, non-intrusive notification (e.g., a green checkmark or a 'Settings saved' message) near the 'Save Settings' button to confirm the action's success.

issues.description: The term "pro/con analysis" might not be familiar to all users, especially those who are not accustomed to formal decision-making processes. This could be confusing for some participants.
issues.recommendation: Replace "Activate pro/con analysis" with a more user-friendly term like "Enable voting on ideas" or "Allow participants to rate ideas". Provide a brief explanation of what this feature does in simpler terms, such as "Let participants vote on the pros and cons of each idea."

issues.description: The term "Activate prioritization" is not clear. It is not obvious what is being prioritized.

issues.description: The term "Phase" is not clear. It is not obvious what is being evaluated.

issues.description: After clicking 'Edit' on the event, the user is taken to a page with many settings and options. If the user accidentally clicks 'Edit' and wants to return to the previous page, there is no clear 'Cancel' or 'Back' button to easily exit the editing mode without making changes.
issues.recommendation: Add a prominent 'Cancel' button or a 'Back' link at the top or bottom of the event editing page to allow users to easily exit the editing mode without saving any changes.

issues.description: When enabling pro/con analysis under 'Decision Support', there is no immediate way to undo this action if the user changes their mind before saving. The user must uncheck the box and save the settings.
issues.recommendation: Consider adding a confirmation dialog when enabling pro/con analysis, giving the user a chance to cancel the action before it's applied. Alternatively, provide a clear visual cue that the setting has been changed but not yet saved, along with a 'Revert' option.

issues.description: The term "Agenda" is used in the tab names and in the settings, but the user renames it to "Destinations". This creates inconsistency in the terminology used throughout the application.
issues.recommendation: After the user renames "Agenda" to "Destinations", the application should consistently use "Destinations" instead of "Agenda" in all relevant sections, including tab names and settings. This will provide a more consistent user experience.

issues.description: The decision support settings use the terms "pro/con analysis" and "prioritization". While related, these are distinct concepts and using both without clear differentiation can be confusing.
issues.recommendation: Clarify the difference between "pro/con analysis" and "prioritization" with a brief explanation next to each option. Alternatively, use a single, overarching term like "decision support methods" and provide more detailed explanations within each method's settings.

issues.description: The phase options in the decision support settings are "Perform evaluation" and "Show results". These terms are not very descriptive and don't clearly indicate what each phase entails.
issues.recommendation: Use more descriptive terms for the phases, such as "Evaluation Phase" and "Results Phase". Provide a brief explanation of what happens in each phase to ensure users understand the process.

issues.description: The 'Activate pro/con analysis' checkbox lacks a clear explanation of its impact on the event planning process. Users might activate it without fully understanding the implications, potentially leading to unintended consequences in how decisions are made.
issues.recommendation: Add a tooltip or a short descriptive text next to the checkbox explaining how activating pro/con analysis will affect the event planning process, including how participants can contribute and how the final decision will be made.

issues.description: The interface does not provide immediate feedback or guidance on how to add ideas for collaborative decision-making after enabling the pro/con analysis. Users might be unsure where to input their suggestions or how to initiate the discussion.
issues.recommendation: After enabling the pro/con analysis, display a brief message or a call-to-action button that directs users to the section where they can add ideas or start a discussion. This could be a link to the 'Agenda' or 'Interesting places' section, depending on the context.

issues.description: The user must navigate through multiple pages (My Events -> Event -> Edit Event -> Decision Support) to enable pro/con analysis, which requires remembering the path and where the setting is located. This increases cognitive load.
issues.recommendation: Provide a direct link or shortcut to the 'Decision Support' settings from the 'My Events' or 'Event' page, or make the pro/con analysis setting more prominent within the event settings.

issues.description: The 'Agenda' section is renamed to 'Destinations' after the user changes it in the settings. However, the user might not immediately recognize that 'Agenda' is where they add destination ideas for the vacation, requiring them to recall the connection between 'Agenda' and 'Destinations'.
issues.recommendation: Provide a brief explanation or tooltip near the 'Destinations' section indicating that this is where destination ideas can be added for the vacation, especially after renaming it from 'Agenda'.

issues.description: The purpose of 'Activate pro/con analysis' and 'Activate prioritization' is not immediately clear without hovering over the information icon. Users must recall or guess what these features do.
issues.recommendation: Provide a short, descriptive label next to each checkbox explaining the functionality of 'pro/con analysis' and 'prioritization' without requiring a hover action. For example, 'Enable voting on pros and cons' and 'Rank destinations based on votes'.

issues.description: The 'Phase' section with 'Perform evaluation' and 'Show results' radio buttons requires the user to understand the different phases of the decision-making process. The user must recall what each phase entails.

issues.description: The term "Agenda" is used as a default name for the section where participants can add ideas for collaborative decision-making. This might not be intuitive for all users, especially those unfamiliar with event planning terminology.
issues.recommendation: Allow the organizer to rename the "Agenda" section to something more descriptive and user-friendly, such as "Destination Ideas" or "Suggestions". This would improve clarity and make the feature more accessible to novice users.

issues.description: The pro/con analysis feature is located under the "Decision Support" tab within the settings, which might not be immediately obvious to users looking for collaborative decision-making tools.

This would improve discoverability and efficiency of use.

issues.description: The tooltips explaining "Activate pro/con analysis" and "Activate prioritization" are helpful but require a hover action. This adds an extra step for users to understand the functionality.
issues.recommendation: Consider providing a brief, static description of the pro/con analysis and prioritization features directly on the settings page, in addition to the tooltips. This would allow users to quickly grasp the functionality without needing to hover over the information icons.

issues.description: The settings page contains many options, some of which might be rarely used. This can overwhelm the user and make it harder to find the desired settings.
issues.recommendation: Consider grouping related settings under collapsible sections or using a progressive disclosure approach to reveal advanced options only when needed. This would declutter the interface and improve usability.

issues.description: The 'Decision Support' settings page contains a lot of text explaining the features. While helpful, it can make the page feel cluttered and less visually appealing.

issues.recommendation: Make the tooltip persistent or provide a link to a dedicated help page with a detailed explanation of the pro/con analysis feature. Consider shortening the tooltip text and providing a link for more information.

issues.description: The "Activate prioritization" option also has an information icon, but it's unclear how prioritization relates to pro/con analysis. Users might need more context to understand the difference and when to use each feature.
issues.recommendation: Clarify the relationship between pro/con analysis and prioritization, either in the tooltip or in a separate help section. Explain when prioritization is useful in addition to or instead of pro/con analysis.

issues.recommendation: After creating a destination entry, display a prominent notification confirming the successful creation and include a direct link back to the main event page within the notification. This will provide immediate feedback and clear navigation.

issues.recommendation: Change the 'Cancel' button text in the confirmation dialog to 'Keep' or 'Don't Remove' to make it clearer that this option will prevent the deletion.

issues.recommendation: Use a consistent structure for success messages. For example, "Destination created successfully" and "Destination updated successfully" would be more consistent and clear.

issues.description: The voting bar is displayed in different colors for each destination. This is inconsistent and does not follow a clear standard.
issues.recommendation: Use a consistent color scheme for the voting bar across all destinations. This will help users easily understand the voting status without being distracted by varying colors.

issues.recommendation: Move the event key input field to a more prominent location, such as near the top of the page, so it is immediately visible to users who want to access the event without creating an account.

issues.description: The event key input field is located at the bottom of the page, requiring users to scroll down to access it. This adds an unnecessary step for users who already have the event key and want to quickly access the event.
issues.recommendation: Move the event key input field to a more prominent location, such as near the top of the page, to allow users to quickly enter the key and access the event without scrolling.

issues.description: The initial landing page contains a lot of information and visual elements that are not directly relevant to the user task of accessing an event with an event key. This can be overwhelming and distracting.
issues.recommendation: Simplify the landing page by prioritizing the event key entry field and reducing the prominence of other elements like the 'Create event' button and the large image. Consider moving less critical information to a separate 'About' or 'Features' page.

issues.description: The event page itself contains a lot of information, some of which might not be immediately relevant to all users. For example, the 'Description' section might be lengthy and not essential for someone just wanting to see the destinations and participants.
issues.recommendation: Consider using progressive disclosure to hide less frequently accessed information. For example, the 'Description' section could be collapsed by default and expanded only when the user clicks a 'Read More' button. This would make the page less cluttered and easier to scan.

heuristic: Help Recognize, Diagnose, Recover from Errors

issues.description: The site lacks a general help section or FAQ to assist users with common questions or troubleshooting. While the interface is relatively straightforward, new users might benefit from a dedicated help area.
issues.recommendation: Implement a help section or FAQ page accessible from the main navigation or footer. This section should address common questions about using the platform, such as creating events, inviting participants, and managing settings.

issues.description: After adding a new destination, the page redirects to the destination's page, but there is no clear visual cue or message indicating that the destination has been successfully added. The user might be confused about whether the action was successful.
issues.recommendation: Display a brief confirmation message (e.g., "Destination added successfully!") at the top of the destination's page after the creation is complete. This provides immediate feedback to the user.

issues.description: When adding a pro or con to a destination, the "Posting has been added successfully" message appears, but it disappears too quickly. The user might miss it, especially if they are focused on other parts of the page.
issues.recommendation: Increase the display time of the "Posting has been added successfully" message to at least 3-5 seconds, or provide a more persistent visual cue, such as highlighting the newly added posting for a short duration.

heuristic: Match between System and Real World

issues.description: The terms "Pro", "Neutral", and "Con" are used to categorize discussion points. While commonly understood, they might not be immediately clear to all users, especially those less familiar with debate terminology.
issues.recommendation: Consider using more descriptive terms like "Good Points", "Unsure", and "Bad Points" or "Advantages", "Neutral", and "Disadvantages" to make the categories more accessible and intuitive.

issues.description: After creating a new destination entry, there is no immediate way to edit the entry directly from the destination's page. The user must navigate back to the main event page and then click the edit icon next to the destination.
issues.recommendation: Add an "Edit" button directly on the destination's page, allowing users to modify the entry without navigating back to the main event page.

issues.description: When adding a pro or con to a destination, there is no 'cancel' button. If a user starts typing and then decides not to post, they must delete the text manually.
issues.recommendation: Include a 'Cancel' button next to the 'Add posting' button in the discussion section to allow users to easily discard their input.

issues.description: When viewing a destination, the 'Back to event' link is at the very bottom of the page, requiring users to scroll down extensively, especially if there are many discussion entries.
issues.recommendation: Add a 'Back to event' link at the top of the destination page as well, providing quicker access to the main event page.

issues.description: The rating system uses different scales across the application. On the destination list, the rating is displayed as a number with two decimal places (e.g., 2.00), while on the destination details page, it's represented by stars. This inconsistency can confuse users about the actual rating value.
issues.recommendation: Standardize the rating system to use either stars or a numerical value consistently throughout the application. If using stars, ensure they accurately reflect the numerical rating. If using numerical values, maintain the same decimal precision across all displays.

issues.description: The 'Add posting' button is used in different contexts with varying visual styles. In the destination creation form, it's a blue button, while in the discussion section of a destination, it's a grey button. This inconsistency can make it harder for users to quickly identify and use the button.
issues.recommendation: Use a consistent visual style for the 'Add posting' button across all contexts. Choose a color and style that is easily recognizable and visually distinct from other elements on the page.

issues.description: The 'Back to event' link is displayed in different locations and with different styles. In the destination creation form, it's at the bottom of the page, while in the destination details page, it's at the top. This inconsistency can make it harder for users to quickly navigate back to the main event page.
issues.recommendation: Standardize the location and style of the 'Back to event' link. Place it in a consistent location, such as the top left corner, and use a consistent visual style, such as a button or a clear text link.

issues.description: When adding a new destination, there is no validation or guidance on the format or type of information expected in the 'Title' field. Users might enter incorrect or incomplete data, leading to confusion or errors later.
issues.recommendation: Implement input validation for the 'Title' field to ensure it contains a valid destination name. Provide a tooltip or placeholder text indicating the expected format (e.g., "City, Country").

issues.description: When adding a new destination, there is no confirmation dialog after clicking the 'Create' button. Users might accidentally create a destination without intending to, or be unsure if the action was successful.
issues.recommendation: Implement a confirmation dialog after the user clicks the 'Create' button, asking them to confirm that they want to add the new destination. This will prevent accidental creation and provide feedback on the action's success.

issues.description: When adding a pro or con to a destination, there is no character limit or warning for the 'Type message...' field. Users might enter excessively long messages, which could negatively impact the display or readability of the discussion.
issues.recommendation: Implement a character limit for the 'Type message...' field and display a warning message as the user approaches the limit. This will prevent excessively long messages and ensure readability.

issues.description: When adding a new destination, the "Contributed by" field only shows the names of the original participants (John Doe and Alice). If another participant, like Bob, adds a destination, their name isn't automatically recognized or suggested, forcing them to recall and manually enter it in the "Name1, Name2, Name3, etc." field.
issues.recommendation: Populate the "Contributed by" field with all participants in the event, allowing the user to select their name from a list instead of manually typing it. This ensures recognition over recall and reduces the chance of errors.

issues.description: When adding a pro or con to a destination, the user has to remember their name and type it into the "Name" field. This requires the user to recall information that the system should already know.
issues.recommendation: Automatically populate the "Name" field with the user's name when they are logged in. This eliminates the need for the user to recall and type their name, improving efficiency and reducing the risk of errors.

issues.description: The interface lacks keyboard shortcuts for common actions like adding a new destination or posting a comment. This slows down experienced users who prefer keyboard navigation.
issues.recommendation: Implement keyboard shortcuts for frequently used actions, such as Ctrl+Enter to submit a comment or Alt+N to add a new destination. Display these shortcuts in tooltips or a help menu.

issues.description: There is no quick way to copy and paste information between destination entries or discussion posts. Users have to manually retype or use the browser's copy-paste functionality, which can be cumbersome.
issues.recommendation: Add a "copy" button to destination entries and discussion posts, allowing users to easily duplicate content. This would be especially useful for copying descriptions or arguments between different destinations.

issues.description: The process of adding a new destination requires scrolling through multiple fields (title, description, link, dates, etc.) even if some are not relevant. This adds unnecessary steps for users who only want to provide basic information.
issues.recommendation: Implement a "quick add" option that only displays the essential fields (title, description). Advanced options like link and dates can be hidden behind an "advanced settings" toggle.

issues.description: The "Contributed by" section on the "Destinations: Create entry" page only shows the names of the original participants, John Doe and Alice, even though the user is adding Bob as a participant. This is confusing and misleading.
issues.recommendation: Dynamically update the "Contributed by" section to reflect all participants involved in the event, including Bob, or remove it entirely as it doesn't seem to serve a clear purpose in this context.

issues.description: The "Name1, Name2, Name3, etc." placeholder text in the "Add selected participants" field is not user-friendly. It's unclear if the user should replace the entire text or add names to it.
issues.recommendation: Replace the placeholder text with a more intuitive instruction, such as "Enter participant names separated by commas" or use a tag-based input field for adding participants.

issues.description: The "Link" field on the "Destinations: Create entry" page defaults to "http://", which is unnecessary and clutters the interface. Most users will likely paste a full URL, making the default prefix redundant.
issues.recommendation: Remove the default "http://" prefix from the "Link" field to simplify the interface and reduce visual clutter.

issues.description: The discussion section on the destination pages has a lot of empty space and the input fields are not well aligned, making it look cluttered and less appealing.
issues.recommendation: Improve the layout of the discussion section by reducing empty space, aligning input fields properly, and using a more visually appealing design for the discussion entries.

heuristic: Help Recognize, Diagnose, Recover from Errors

issues.description: When adding a new destination, there is no validation or error message if required fields like 'Title' or 'Description' are left blank. The 'Create' button simply does nothing, leaving the user unsure why the destination wasn't added.
issues.recommendation: Implement client-side validation to check for required fields before submitting the form. Display clear error messages next to the empty fields, indicating what needs to be filled in.

issues.description: When adding a new discussion posting, if the user forgets to select either 'Pro', 'Neutral', or 'Con', the 'Add posting' button still shows a success message, but the posting is not actually added. This gives the user false feedback.
issues.recommendation: Implement validation to ensure that a 'Pro', 'Neutral', or 'Con' option is selected before allowing the posting to be added. Display an error message if none is selected.
